name: Tawang Monastery (Galden Namgyal Lhatse)
description: Largest Buddhist monastery in India and second-largest in the world, founded in 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso under the guidance of the 5th Dalai Lama. Perched at about 10,000 ft overlooking the Tawang Chu valley, it houses a 28-foot gilded Buddha statue, ancient manuscripts, and is the spiritual heart of the Monpa people. Home to over 500 monks of the Gelug school.
facts: Founded 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso
Largest monastery in India; second-largest worldwide
Birthplace region of the 6th Dalai Lama

name: Sela Pass
description: High-altitude mountain pass at 4,170 m (13,700 ft) on the border of Tawang and West Kameng districts. Gateway to Tawang on NH-13, often snow-covered, with Sela Lake (Paradise Lake) nearby. Offers dramatic Himalayan views and is a key stop en route to Tawang.
facts: On NH-13 connecting Tawang to the rest of India
Border between Tawang and West Kameng districts
Sela Tunnel provides all-weather connectivity below the pass

name: Nuranang Falls (Jang Falls)
description: Spectacular 100-metre high waterfall near Jang town, about 40 km from Tawang on the route from Sela Pass. Originates from the northern slopes of Sela Pass; features a small hydel plant at the base. Popular stop for photography amid lush forests.
facts: Also known as Bong Bong Falls or Jung Falls
Fed by Nuranang Chu from Sela Pass slopes

name: Sangetsar Tso (Madhuri Lake)
description: High-altitude glacial lake formed by an earthquake, famous for dead tree trunks rising from its crystal-clear waters. Located on the road toward Bum La Pass, about 17-35 km from Tawang. Popularly known as Madhuri Lake after a Bollywood song shoot.
facts: Also called Madhuri Lake or Shonga-tser Lake
Formed by seismic activity with submerged forest
On the route to Bum La Pass

name: Bum La Pass
description: Border pass at 4,600 m (15,200 ft) on the India-China Line of Actual Control, about 37 km from Tawang. Historic trade route and 1962 war site; requires special Army/district permit for Indian visitors. Offers high-altitude views and is a Border Personnel Meeting point.
facts: Route used by 14th Dalai Lama in 1959

name: Urgelling Monastery
description: Historic monastery founded in 1489, recognized as the birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama Tsangyang Gyatso. Smaller and quieter than Tawang Monastery, located near Tawang town with traditional Tibetan architecture and spiritual significance for Monpa heritage.

name: Tawang War Memorial
description: Memorial stupa dedicated to Indian soldiers who died in the 1962 Sino-Indian War. Located in Tawang town area, it lists names of the fallen and serves as a site of remembrance with panoramic valley views.

name: Tawang Town
description: District headquarters and main tourist base in Tawang district at about 3,000 m elevation. Gateway for exploring the monastery, passes, and lakes; features markets, hotels, and Monpa cultural elements. Requires Inner Line Permit for visitors.
facts: Base for ILP holders exploring the region

name: Jaswant Garh War Memorial
description: War memorial honoring Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat of the 4th Garhwal Rifles for his bravery in the 1962 Battle of Nuranang. Located en route between Sela Pass and Tawang near Jang, at high altitude with military significance.

name: Pankang Teng Tso (PT Tso)
description: High-altitude lake about 16-18 km from Tawang on the Bum La road, often frozen in winter. Offers serene alpine scenery amid mountains; accessible with Bum La route permit.
facts: Also called PT Tso or Pangang Teng Tso
On the road toward Bum La Pass
